children: Shares of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery were higher after The Wall Street Journal reported that Paramount has discussed potential concessions with California's attorney general to clear the $81 billion merger between the two companies.
Shares of Paramount were up 6.7% to $10.89 in pre-market trading on Monday. Warner Bros. shares gained 7.6% to $29.90.

The talks to settle a lawsuit by a coalition of states seeking to block the deal on antitrust grounds have included the possibility of Paramount making a $1.5 billion investment in production in California, the Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Other concessions on the table involve Paramount promising not to sell either company's studio lot or move out of the state, the Journal reported, adding that the company had explored a move out of California as the deal ran into opposition.

The talks have also included penalties for Paramount failing to fulfill its pledge of making 30 movies a year post-merger, including selling its stake in Miramax, as well as the sale of some cable channels and a board to oversee CNN's editorial independence, according to the Journal.
No deal has been finalized and it is unclear which terms the parties will agree to, the Journal reported.
In addition to the coalition of states, the Writers Guild of America has sued to block the deal on antitrust grounds.
